reviews.text: One of the best hiking spots in china. There are 4 gates via which you can visit the forest but the most popular one is east gate due to avatar Mountains and the fastest elevator. You can buy passed according to which gate and cable car you want to take. Unfortunately I was there on a cloudy day but even then the mystic vibe gave it a good touch.

What a breathtaking place! crazy what nature can create and how impressive these formations look in real. Also really recommend taking the 6km long golden whip stream path and walk through the valley to get a view of these giants from below! went in mid November (Thursday and Friday), weather was decent and not as crowded as I expected. There was never any waiting lines at the cable cars or elevator, just make sure you make your bookings for the preferred time at least a day before.

Truly a wonderful park, Avatar has chosen well its filming location . I have never seen such kind of mountains anywhere in the West. It is well organized despite the crowd w a lot of food and drink places along the way, shuttle buses to take you from one to the next place on a constant schedule. It is super clean, the paths unlike national parks in the west are all paved and with steps. You won’t find a gravel road to walk on. Do spend 2 days exploring it. 1 day, enter from the East Gate and head to the direction of the world’s highest outdoor elevator, visit clockwise, don’t forget to visit Terrace in the sky which costs extra. Walk all the way down, there is a drone photographer who can have a fantastic drone film 98 cny made for you without the crowd anywhere else you encounter in the park. The 2nd day do Huangshizai enter from the South Gate take the cable up walk clockwise. After you come down, I would definitely walk all 7km along the creek and exit from the east gate. Along the creek you will have the park almost to yourself as not many tourists do the long walk and you will encounter the snow monkey cousins. We went very early the 1st day to avoid the crowd, but the fog hasn’t cleared up. I would probably enter around 9:30-10 if it is a good day because by then the fogs would be gone. You have to decide whether you want the long wait or the fog. Have fun.

We visited the park the last day of November and first day of December and the crowds were very low. We didn’t have to queue for almost anything which is a big deal in China. Only the most famous spots (hallelujah mountains etc) were very crowded with tour groups, screaming people using speakers and so on but once you walk further away it got better. We enjoyed most the south and south west part of the park which requires more walking and it had way less crowds and noise. It was so relaxing and peaceful and had almost no tour groups. I would easily spent 2-3 days exploring the park. We got the tickets from our hotel with a discount and only spent 2 full days in the park. I’d say get some snacks with you because although there are many vendors selling food and snacks they can be a bit more expensive, not too bad though. We had our own snacks but had lunch in the park. Also bring your own toilet paper and soap for the hands because don’t have any unfortunately which is a shame for such a big park they accepts so many tourists daily.

​If you want a physical challenge with a spiritual reward, Tianmen Cave is the place to be. Standing at the base and looking up at that massive natural arch is truly humbling—it feels like a portal to another world! ​The Experience: The climb up the 999 steps is no joke! It’s steep and will definitely get your heart racing, but there are platforms along the way to catch your breath and take in the view. If you’re not feeling up for the hike, there’s actually a series of escalators inside the mountain that can take you to the top, but there’s a special sense of accomplishment in taking the stairs. ​Why it’s worth it: ​The Scale: Once you reach the "Gate," the sheer size of the archway is incredible. You can feel the wind rushing through the mountain. ​The Photo Ops: Looking back down the staircase toward the valley provides one of the most dramatic views in all of China. ​The Journey: To get here, you usually take a bus up the 99 Bends Road, which is a thrill ride in itself! ​Pro Tip: Try to visit on a clear day if possible. When it’s too foggy, the "hole" completely disappears into the clouds. Also, wear shoes with good grip—those stone steps can get slippery when damp! ​A must-visit for anyone traveling through Hunan. It’s exhausting, beautiful, and absolutely unforgettable. ⛩️✨ ​#TianmenMountain #HeavensGate #Zhangjiajie #ChinaTravel #StairwayToHeaven #TravelChina

Probably one of the greatest days I’ve spent on my 3 week China Trip were in this National Park. I stayed in the YOLO resort. It’s actually IN the park itself and has a great community. Don’t be affraid to talk and make friends to other people in the Resort. Seize the Day. Talk to the locals. All in all Great. Experience and huge National park. I‘ll attach some pictures I took in the Park.

Planned our visit for late October and opted for the fast-track option, which we definitely appreciated when we zoomed past 10 minute queues which gave us more time exploring the landmarks. The ride up on the cable car is exhilarating and truly milestone memorable!! We made our way down by the touristy spots, which were busy, but if you were willing to walk 10 minutes away, you were rewarded with the most magnificent views of Mother Nature's rock skyscrapers and the mist drifting amidst the tree-lined stacks! The elevator down definitely tested my vertigo-nerves, but is a feat of engineering that can't be missed. We finished off our visit at the beautiful river and little 6km train ride where we were entertained by the resident monkeys and their thieving mischief.

Multiple vantage points to view one of the most geographically spectacular sites on the planet. Many entry points and various options to travel around the park. Cable cars, busses operating regularly and efficiently. None of the on-site staff speak any English, which seems unusual for an international destination, so consider hiring a guide. Not one of the cheapest Chinese tourists places.

Let me say that you must come here and not read any reviews. Just show up and see for yourself what magic this place beholds. No wonder the Monkey God used to dwell this land. It’s clearly the best place for training high level Wing Chun.

Zhangjiajie National Forest park 张家界国家森林公园 is where Mother Nature built skyscrapers before humans even figured out bricks. Recognized as the first national forest park in China (1982) and part of the larger 武陵源 UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992, it’s officially rated a 5A tourist attraction, which in China means expect world-class views and equally world-class crowds. Even in off season it feels like half the country decided to go hiking with you. Main areas to explore before your legs give up: • 金鞭溪 Golden Whip Stream – a tranquil valley walk with towering cliffs, crystal-clear water, and monkeys plotting to steal your snacks. • 袁家界 Yuanjiajie – home of the iconic Avatar Hallelujah Mountain where sandstone pillars levitate in misty glory. • 杨家界 Yangjiajie – dramatic cliffs and quieter trails, great for pretending you discovered Zhangjiajie before everyone else. • 黄石寨 Huangshizhai – panoramic viewpoints so good that locals say “if you don’t climb Huangshizhai, you haven’t truly seen Zhangjiajie.” • 十里画廊 Ten Mile Gallery – stone peaks arranged like a giant natural scroll painting. Spoiler: it feels shorter than ten miles. • 张家界大峡谷 Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon – home to dizzying cliffs, waterfalls, and the record-breaking Glass Bridge, which is basically a test of whether you trust both physics and your legs. Pro tip If you don’t like spending more time in queues than on trails, get the VIP ticket. It skips the lines for elevators, cable cars, and shuttle buses.. saving up to an hour per attraction. Worth it when you realize standing in a queue here is the only view not worth photographing. Five stars because 张家界国家森林公园 is essentially nature’s IMAX in 4D.. mist, monkeys, and mild vertigo included, plus tourists everywhere waving selfie sticks like bamboo spears trying to capture the same mountain from 37 slightly different angles.

This place got so famous because of the Avatar movie, but it is really amazing in real life! You can't capture the beauty in any photo. Seeing it in person is so cool! The mountains are so thin and long, unlike anything I've ever seen anywhere else. There is a lot of walking here so be prepared. We went during the winter time so it got foggy for us. I would recommend coming here in Feb or March if you want to avoid the huge crowds and heat.

A stunning and unique park, now a popular tourist destination for those traveling to China. Everything is very clean and organized, and you'll find yourself immersed in nature, enjoying breathtaking views. Take the elevator up to the top of the sandstone peaks and enjoy the view. You have to be lucky and find a sunny day.

I’m from Malaysia and came here on 25 January 2026. There was no snowfall, but it was extremely cold—I had to wear 4–5 layers. It was quite tiring because we went up by bus, and there were four buses involved, plus a lot of steps to climb. We went down by cable car (actually, you can go both up and down by cable car). Unfortunately, the view from the top wasn’t very clear because of thick fog. The best view I got was actually from the bottom.

14-18/10/2025 Zhangjiajie Trip We set off from Hong Kong by high-speed rail. this journey was having to book high-speed rail tickets 14 days in advance on 12306 The weather didn’t cooperate—it was either rainy or overcast for all five days. For the first two days, we stayed at the Ji Hotel全季酒店 near 東門Dongmen, just a 3-minute walk from the Dongmen Gate. Through the hotel, we booked the main entrance tickets and a combo ticket for the three cable cars and one elevator (¥191 for seniors over 65 and ¥480 for one adult, plus Tianmen Mountain Route A tickets for ¥116 + ¥268). Since we entered at 7:30 a.m., there weren’t many people. We took the eco-friendly bus to the Bailong Elevator, and just as I arrived, the queue was cut off right in front of me, allowing me to be the first to enter the elevator. The weather wasn’t great, so we just wandered around casually. On the second day, we entered through the south gate and took the cable car up to 黃石寨Huangshi Village to see the peaks. Perhaps it was still early, but the mist hadn’t cleared yet, and a light drizzle was falling. We couldn’t see any peaks clearly, so we had no choice but to head back down and look for the "Monkey King." Unfortunately, even the monkeys weren’t out. Luckily, we spotted three of them just as we were about to give up. We then took a taxi to the Tianmen Mountain Hotel, dropped off our luggage, and went to explore the 72奇楼.

OMG if you haven’t yet been to Zhangjiajie Forest, put it on your radar. From the top of the mountains is the most spectacular view. Incredible scenery from every viewpoint. Quite a bit of walking involved but totally worth it. Try and get a drone video done as the result is a top quality video with amazing scenery.

Simply amazing, wonderful. If you ever get the opportunity to visit, I highly recommend you go. The whole area including Wulingyuan and glass bridge you should be able to cover in 4 days. I recommend you try walking to the top, climbing the stairs and meeting many monkeys along the way. It took us 2.5 hours to climb up and 2 hours to go down. It was well worth the effort (plus we like hiking). Highly recommend you bring DEET or insect repellant and a good pair of broken-in walking shoes.

This is an amazing place to visit. Well worth the effort to get there. It is busy if you just go where the buses take you. But you can avoid the crowds by walking. For example, when following Golden Whip stream you will hardly see any other people.

The national forest park is very nice it is unique in its kind. I really recommend it if you want to see nice nature. But before going there you should plan your itinerary to save time and see most of the park. I recommend taking the cable car if you only take one day to visit the park, but all tickets are for 4 days. You have buses inside that bring you everywhere but you can also walk. The negative part is that all the Paths are delimited which means you can’t really explore new places or get lost in the park.

This national forest park is made famous by the movie Avatar and caters to hordes of tourists. It is China;s first national forest park and listed on Unesco World Natural Heritage site. The spectacular beauty and landscape is worth a visit. The sandstones pillars are breathtaking and lots of walking should be expected here.

Zhangjiajie National Forest Park features a dramatic landscape with towering stunning sandstone pillars , misty mountains and hidden valleys. Lots of walking, from the challenging hikes on the Golden Whip Stream to more relaxed cable car and Bailong Sky elevator ride. This Park was full with visitors, thus navigating through the crowd for photography can be challenging, Every popular view points are taken up by their local photographers too. Despite dealing with crowds, I must say the views of these iconic floating which inspired the making of Movie Avatar are amazing. Simply unforgettable views making it a must see for the fans of the film.
The view here is absolutely stunning—there’s really no need to explain why it’s worth visiting, the photos speak for themselves. The toilet facilities are also clean and well-maintained.

Beautiful park, famous for its filming location for Avatar. Unfortunately, it was a rainy day when I came here following tour. Although it does give a mysterious feel with the fog, but at the peak, cant take any pictures because of the fog! its a pity though.

Words and photos are too poor to describe breathtaking views in the park. We visited on 7-8 th of July 2025. First day arrived to Wulingyuan gate at 12pm, bought entrance and unlimited cable cars tickets onsite. Route to Tianzi, roughly 45 min line to cable car. Then 2 shuttle buses 30 min to Yuanjiajie scenic area, Avatar mountain, various viewing platforms and other sights. Then bus to south gate, cable car and long walk through the park to taxi area. Day 2 arrived at 14 with hope for no line for Bailong, and we were lucky - walked straight in. In july path between Hallelujah mountain and Bailong was closed, so to ride elevator you have to take shuttle bus from entrance, elevator up and down and bus back to entrance ( Wulingyuan). I heard about crowds and lines for each shuttle bus and attraction in the morning, so we chose to come in afternoon. Less crowded, no lines for buses, you can easily take pictures alone. Honestly unlimited rides are not a must, to make it worth it we took Yuangjiajie cable car 3 times 😅

Zhangjiajie national forest park is an amazing place! You have these peaks made of limestone rock that just jut out of the ground going straight up to form majestic shafts of rugged beauty! I believe it's this place that helped inspire the world of Avatar the movie. This place is just breathtaking!

Absolutely spectacular scenery and wonders of nature. This place has been exposed to the world by genius design of the extraordinary infrastructure that made it possible to access this place. The whole GEOPARK is beautifully managed and provides great facilities.

The natural beauty of this park is terrific, but our experience at the bailong lift was hot, muggy, and so crowded we could barely see anything worth standing in line for. We had clearer views from elsewhere in the park. Ticketing is confusing and overpriced compared to other global natural parks. When I tried to get on the bus to exit the park, the face ID scanner did not work. One of the park personnel was rude with me, yelling "GO" without taking a moment to understand that the machine was not working. There are many beautiful parks in the world where I have not been yelled at, or stood in non air conditioned lines. We paid $140 USD for full tickets to the park, where other national parks (without this kind of crowd) have charged me less than $20 for nicer walks. This park is beautiful but it is not ready for global tourism.
Wonderful park. The one to visit when in Zhangjiajie. Tickets are valid for four days although 2 days would definitely suffice depending on your style and pace of visit

Spending a full day at Zhangjiajie National Forest Park—from morning all the way into the evening—was one of the most surreal and unforgettable experiences I’ve had. If you’re someone who loves nature, mountains, and feeling completely surrounded by something much bigger than yourself, this is the place. From the moment I arrived in the morning, the air felt fresh and calming. The park is incredibly vast, and every corner offers something different—tall sandstone pillars rising through the mist, quiet forest paths, hidden waterfalls, and panoramic viewpoints that genuinely make you stop and just breathe it all in. I started the day walking along Golden Whip Stream, and the calmness of the water combined with the towering cliffs was the perfect way to ease into the park. Midday, I took the Bailong Elevator up to Yuanjiajie, and that view? Unreal. It felt like stepping into a dream—or a movie set. It’s easy to see why Avatar used this place for inspiration. The “floating mountains” really do look like they defy gravity. As the day went on, the clouds shifted, the lighting changed, and the park just kept transforming. By late afternoon, I was up at the Tianzi Mountain area, watching the layers of peaks fade into the distance. It was quiet, peaceful, and seriously hard to look away. I stayed until the last possible moment. As evening settled in and the crowds thinned out, it became even more magical—like I had the park to myself. The mist returned, and everything felt still. What I loved: – The variety: calm streams, dramatic cliffs, forest trails, and sky-high views – The fact that the park changes throughout the day—you’ll want to stay as long as possible – Even with so many people visiting, it still felt peaceful and immersive – Great mix of walking trails, shuttles, and elevators—so it’s manageable even with all the exploring Pro Tips: – Get there early to beat the crowds and catch the morning light – Bring snacks and water—it’s a full-day kind of adventure – Don’t try to rush it—Zhangjiajie is meant to be savored slowly – Dress in layers, the weather shifts fast up in the mountains This wasn’t just a sightseeing stop—it was an all-day experience that made me feel connected to nature in the deepest way. I left tired, full of photos, and already wanting to come back. If you’re going to do one thing in China that makes you feel like you’re on another planet—this is it.

Recommend visiting in the offseason for minimal crowds. You can realistically see everything in 2 days if the weather is good. Expect to use the busses and cable cars a lot, there is not that much of a hiking feel. The landscapes are very nice tho

A must see when visiting Zhangjiajie. The views are spectacular, and breathtaking. For the amount of people that come through the park, it is very well organized. You must have patience dealing with large crowds. Every view point is pushing and shoving. Be prepared to put on a good pair of walking shoes, and get ready to climb many steps. I came after the national holiday, and was still very busy. I wouldn't recommend visiting during any holiday dates.

Amazing place! To fully explore the site, I would recommend about 3 days for Zhangjiajie Park. The one extra day you can do The Canyon (I higly recommend it) and which is located about 40km from Zhangjiajie Park. For the Park itself, I recommend the option- entrance for 4days/all included. That way you can use buses/cablecars and elevator for unlimited time. Bare in mind that the Park is alway full ofv visitors, hence for some attractions etc the queues are pretty long... The one solution for that-vip entrance (always worth to try if you dont mind to spend some extra money)

I visited Zhangjiajie with my family and engaged a local tour for our trip. Based on my experience, I strongly recommend opting for a private tour. Unlike standard group tours, private tours won’t pressure you to visit and spend at tourist souvenir shops, which can be quite stressful. From what I understand, many tour guides rely on commissions from these shops as they don’t receive a fixed salary. That said, the overall experience of sightseeing in Zhangjiajie was absolutely worth it. The stunning landscapes and unique attractions make it a destination I would highly recommend to anyone planning a trip to China!

In Aug 2024, it was super hot and super crowded, but it did not take much away from the absolutely spectacular beauty all around Zhangjiajie. The tall elevator was fun. The "needles" were incredible, and you get pretty close to them. We took the 2000 stairs path down to the valley and that ended up being a great call, the temperatures drop as you enter the green spaces, the crowds disappear, and you end up next to a cool river with immense monkeys entertainment!
Breathtaking! Took the elevator up to the top of the mountain to visit the floating Avatar Hallelujah Mountains and the “The First Bridge Under Heaven” 天下第一桥

By far my favourite national park in China. This is a great place to hike, I recommand hiking and not taking elevators with too much tourists. You will be alone in the mountain with monkeys, trully incredible

Amazed by the scenery of the nature! It was a bit of regret as it was a sunny day and we were not able to see the cloud with the mountain! But was lucky enough as we can still see the mountain! No complaint. The air and the scenery makes me feel really happy for no reason. There is plenty of weird monkey and happen that the monkey snatch the plastic bag of the tourist.

Zhangjiajie National Forest Park is a majestic slice of heaven perfect for the nature lovers. It is a world heritage park that features a lot of awesome mountain views. It is a friendly trek for young and old alike. To reach the peak, you do not have to sweat it out. The walk is minimal. There are buses at different stations that will bring you up and going down is easy peasy with a bus and an 8 minute cable ride and the fall colors of the trees are just awesome when you view it from the cable car. There are also food vendors at the top that sells a lot of Chinese street foods. And wonder of wonders, there is even KFC and Starbucks. My photos do not do it justice at all.

This is a must in everyone's bucket list! As it's off season, there was very little queuing. We booked through trip.com, very fuss free and with a tour guide who will pick u from your hotel. Highly recommend getting a tour guide, this place is huge! There are so much to do and see. Without a guide we will definitely waste alot of time moving around. Tip : Avoid the monkeys, they are very aggressive and will grab anyone with any plastic bags in sight!

Unforgettable experience. This is one of the top 5 national forest park in 🇨🇳. The view of the pillar mountains are magnificent, it is no comparison to any wonders you have seen from this planet. If you ever go to blue mountain in NSW 🇦🇺, it will make blue mountain looks like a dwarf, it's like comparing the 3 sisters ⛰️ to a thousand sisters ⛰️. If you have a chance, be sure to put in your 🪣 list. 😊 holiday and Sight 👀

The national park is a piece of natural beauty. It certainly leaves you awestruck. Tickets are valid for 4 days which means you can visit unlimited times during the validity. However, attractions like bailong elevator, cable cars are all paid separately unless purchased with the unlimited access package. the park has signboard in English, bus stations are well marked and there are maps too. We did our study and were able to easily navigate without the need of a guide. It took us an entire day to cover the main sites and we totally loved our experience. The avatar mountains, bailong elevator, tianzi mountain, cableways are all fantastic and amazing.

A must see! Beautiful place and there are busses that go to different parts of the park so you don’t have to walk everywhere(there is still quite a lot of walking you need to do though). Gets very crowded at some places so bets ready for that. It is quite high up and there are a lot of shaded places so it doesn’t get unbearably hot. I would recommend to buy the ticket before hand so you do to queue for that. The ticket is valid for 4 days and I would recommend you to go there for atleast 2 days if you want to see everything. I was there for 1 day and I could not see the whole place, but the most important things!

Incredible national Park with vertical rock formations that inspired Avatar. South and Southeast entrances are easiest and least crowded - need one day for each. Get the unlimited pass to use all the rides, and enjoy! There are plenty of vendors and restrooms, but bring your own toilet paper.
Zhangjiajie is a beautiful national park with a big biodiversity, and amazing landscapes, the only downside is the amount of people that visit the park everyday

Zhangjiajie is very senior-friendly if you focus on Yuanjiajie and Tianzi Mountain, both accessible by cable car and the Bailong Elevator, with mostly flat walking paths and beautiful Avatar-style scenery. Baofeng Lake is the easiest spot—flat walking and a relaxing boat ride. Seniors with good mobility can also enjoy Tianmen Mountain using the long cable car and escalators (everywhere) to avoid stairs. This at least 3-day route is scenic, comfortable, and low-stress for older travelers.

The absolute highlight of our China trip! You really have the feeling to be in the Avatar Movie Great walks and amazing scenery. Once in the Park you can hike many trails or catch the free buses to navigate the Park. Easy to spend 3 days exploring. The tickets you buy for about 60$ is valid for 3 days.

Zhangjiajie National Forest Park is located in China's Hunan Province. It's famous for its towering sandstone pillars, lush vegetation, and scenic beauty. The park inspired the floating mountains in the movie Avatar. It's renowned for its breathtaking natural landscapes, including the Bailong Elevator, Tianmen Mountain, and the glass skywalk. The park offers various activities like hiking, sightseeing, and photography, attracting tourists from around the world. There is Direct Bus From 0600hrs 1730hrs (every hours ) Zhangjiajie Bus Station. 🚉 Ticket cost Is 12 RMB. It’s takes about 1 hours. Park tickets is 227 RMB which is valid for 4 Days. It’s Recommended visit at least 3 Days to Explore the Park. Map Is little confusing but you have manage at own.

China is gorgeous, and Zhangjiajie is one of the most amazing places you can visit. Even though it is not easy to visit, as you need to take the plane or high speed train because it is far, it is totally worth it. It was not easy to plan the park beforehand, but when you have the local maps from the hotel, it becomes easy. I cannot recommend Zhangjiajie enough, you have to visit once in your life. It is famous from the movie Avatar.

Zhangjiajie National Forest Park is probably the most coveted part of the area. The park is comprised of dense forests, deep ravines, deep canyons, unusual peaks, caves, and pillar-like rock formations blanketed throughout the park. These pillar rock formations are what the park is renowned for around the world.

I Highly recommend getting the unlimited cable car ride pass and riding each cable line several times, up and back. This place is so beautiful you simply cannot stand and take it all in. Make sure to walk along the Gold Whip stream. I’d highly recommend walking down to gold whip stream from the avatar (hallelujah) mountains. This gets you away from the tourists and gives you great views of the peaks as you descend down to the valley. We are English speaking only and we’re able to find our away around, make sure to get a white paper map and keep with you because the maps posted on the brown signs throughout the park are SO confusing. But the large folding white map from the info kiosks were great. We bought the pass that gave you unlimited bus rides, elevator, and cable rides. It was 518 rmb per person. We did the math and everything we wanted to do was cheaper, but are very thankful we decided not to pinch pennys and got the unlimited because travel time to each attraction took a while (riding bus and walking, so it was nice to ride the elevator and cable rides over and over while we were there. Also, the shuttle bus system here was amazing. Lines are long but they move fast, just like an amusement park.

A stunning, breathtaking and awe-inspiring place. The inspiration for Pandora in the Avatar movie. An absolute must-see. The best time to see will be in early winter as the place will appear mythical and magical in the mist. The park comprised of dense forests, deep ravines, deep canyons, unusual peaks, caves, and pillar-like rock formations blanketed throughout the park. These pillar rock formations are what the park is renowned for around the world.

This is probably one of the coolest places I have visited. There are breathtaking photos at every turn! We hiked a lot with our guide, and it was truly something I will remember forever. Some trails are on the cliffs and are amazing to see.

Excellent tourist attractions. Biggest elevator is here Good transport facilities. Nice elevators. Good ambience Lot's of crowd. Bus service is good If weather is good. You can enjoy. Good washroom One must visit it. Look for bailong elevator
Beautiful, once a life time must visit to Zhangjiajie national park and Furong Ancient Town.

Zhangjiajie National Forest Park is breathtaking! The stunning natural scenery, towering sandstone pillars, and lush greenery make it a truly magical place. The trails are well-maintained, and the views are unforgettable. A must-visit for nature lovers and adventurers. Highly recommend!

Huge complex of mountains where you will have to travel by shuttle buses, cable car, even take a lift high as Eifel Tower :-) The mountains are breathtaking and unforgettable. Thanks to Avatar movies it gets more popular and I think that’s a good thing, otherwise I think we will maybe not have visited this place and it will be a mistake. If you are not sure to come because it’s maybe far, you definitely should come, it’s worthy to travel here. The tickets are for 4 days. We only have 1,5 day and still worthy, worthy, worthy :-)

This place was very beautiful and awesome scenery, it's one of the movie scenery shots (Avatar) Walk way and climbing staircase is far and long but worth to have a look and take pictures, air is very fresh. Food store and toilet only available at the upper mountain there (middle of the walking trip) Cons: This place not well maintain and less security guard. Beware of cutting queue and pushing you from the back while crouded, usually those old folks. Those old folks are very rude and unpolite.

Easy and nice hikes, no need to take cable cars or the elevator. I would recommend to spend at least three full days here to cover the whole area. It's crucial to start in the early morning to escape the tourist masses ;) If you decided to hike instead of taking the cable cars, you are mostly alone, but the main spots are pretty crowded. You can have equally good views just a bit of the track, so there is no point in waiting in line to get a picture from the spots which are close to the cable car stations. Orientation is easy, signs are everywhere

迷魂台 is a must go when you vist zjj national forest. It is where Avatar movie is shot. The view is breathtaking. Very spectacular and enchanting. Love every minute of it when i was there. The last video is taken from inside of the 百龙天梯. Totally love the view and experience!

Wow, this place is magical. The scenery is on another, if you really wanna enjoy this place I recommend not taking cable car and elevator, walk everywhere. The crowds thin out when walking deeper inside. And that's when you can really take it slow and enjoy this place. Because the main spots are way too crowded and you'll get overwhelmed by local tour groups. Also great organisation by the staff to take us to and back from the bus.

Zhangjiajie National Park is an absolute marvel, boasting some of the most breathtaking views on the planet. From towering sandstone pillars shrouded in mist to lush valleys carpeted with emerald foliage, every corner of the park is a feast for the eyes. The sheer scale and otherworldly beauty of the landscape leave visitors in awe, making it a photographer's dream and a paradise for nature lovers. One of the park's main attractions is its network of hiking trails, offering visitors the chance to immerse themselves in its pristine wilderness. Whether trekking along winding pathways that lead to panoramic viewpoints or venturing deep into the heart of the forest, each hike is an adventure filled with discovery and wonder. The diversity of terrain ensures there's something for hikers of all skill levels, from leisurely strolls to more challenging expeditions. Beyond its natural wonders, Zhangjiajie is also steeped in cultural significance, with ancient temples and cultural landmarks scattered throughout the park. These historical sites add depth to the visitor experience, offering insights into the region's rich heritage. In summary, Zhangjiajie National Park is a testament to the beauty and power of nature, offering visitors the chance to witness landscapes that seem straight out of a fairy tale. English/Australian couple touring China, we travelled to Zhangjiajie airport and got a transfer to our accommodation (Purespace) located a short walk to the Zimugang entrance to the National Park. This entrance is quieter than the main South Entrance. Tickets last 4 days from purchase, and buses take you round the park. We found that the buses work in a hop on-hop off fashion (I.e. you can’t stay on one bus all the way round). We recommend taking a photo of the Chinese spelling of the entrance / exit so that you can show park employees (very minimal English is spoken!). We love the outdoors and hiking, and quickly learnt that you can avoid crowds of local tourists by walking deeper into the park. Our 2 day itinerary we discovered which we loved: Day 1) From Zimugang gate, get the bus to the Bialong Elevator (don’t even bother taking it - it’s crowded and you have to pay extra!), then hop on the bus back to Golden Whip stream (the stop between Zimugang and Bialong). From here, walk along the stream until you get to a staircase on the right. This is up to Avatar mountain, a long walk but worth it! No tourists, saw lots of wildlife (including monkeys) and amazing views at the top. There are ways (buses/walking) back down but we were funnelled into the elevator which we had to pay for. It wasn’t worth it, crowded and too fast to take in scenery! Day 2) We got to Zimugang gate at 8:45am - no tourists there! We took the bus to Golden Whip and then hopped on the bus to Ten Mile Gallery. Beautiful scenery (despite the tram running along the path for the first 1.5km!) After then, you walk up the stairs for about 2 hours until you get to a McDonalds (!) at the base of the Tianzi pavilion. We didn’t see a single person on the stairs, it was peaceful and so atmospheric. From the road at the top, we took the bus to the cable car and took that down the mountain which I highly recommend! From there we got the bus back to 10 mile gallery - Golden Whip - Zimugang. We didn’t do the tourist spots like the Stairway to Heaven (Tianzi mountain), nor the glass bottomed bridge… and we don’t regret it!

REVIEW FOR A ONE DAY VISIT If you're planning to see the maximum of Zhangjiajie in just one day and furthermore trying to avoid the crowd, I recommend taking the following itinerary : Start early (the park opens at 7AM) Arrive at Forest Park gate. Take the cable car to Yellow stone Village and start the walk around the plateau. You'll have nice views without the crowds. Take the cable car down and continue your way following the golden whip stream until you reach the intersection going to Yuanjiajie scenic area. It is a climb up, but the views above are wonderful. Follow the path further to reach the main highlights (hallelujah mountains and the first natural bridge). Then go down to the bus station and take the bus to Sancha (direction of Tianzishan, 2nd stop). Then take an Electric bus to the Rice fields on top of the mountain. Beautiful sight, but difficult to assess by foot. Take the Electric bus back to Sancha. If you have time left, you can walk the way (street) up to the 'grand viewing platform' . No tourists to be seen and a nice view. Then take the bus at Sancha to Tianzishan. If you have 2h-3h left you can walk down and take the bus at the end of 10mile gallery to the entrance. If not, take the cable car at Tianzishan down and then the bus to the entrance. Have a nice one!

Zhangjiajie National Forest Park stands as an extraordinary natural wonder, offering visitors an otherworldly landscape that seems straight out of a fantasy film. This park represents a highlight of any China journey, showcasing some of the most unique and spectacular scenery on Earth. The park's gigantic scale is breathtaking, featuring towering sandstone pillars that pierce through the mists, creating an almost mystical atmosphere. These iconic formations, which famously inspired the floating mountains in the movie Avatar, demonstrate nature's ability to create truly remarkable landscapes. The extensive network of trails, cable cars, and elevators allows visitors to explore different perspectives of this magnificent park. Whether viewing the formations from below or enjoying panoramic vistas from elevated platforms, each angle offers a new and stunning view of these natural wonders. The park's ability to shift its appearance throughout the day, as mists roll through the peaks and sunlight plays across the rock faces, ensures that no two visits are exactly alike. This ever-changing landscape keeps visitors enchanted throughout their exploration. While not explicitly mentioned, the park likely offers various amenities and services to support extended visits, allowing tourists to fully immerse themselves in this natural spectacle. For anyone planning a trip to China, Zhangjiajie National Forest Park should be considered an essential destination. Its unique landscape and awe-inspiring scale make it a truly unforgettable experience that showcases the incredible natural beauty China has to offer.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Zhangjiajie – The World That Inspired Avatar Visiting the Avatar Mountains in Zhangjiajie National Forest Park was one of the most breathtaking experiences I've ever had. Here's what stood out: Landscapes: The towering sandstone pillars truly resemble the floating islands from Avatar. These incredible formations were sculpted by nature over millions of years, and their beauty is mesmerizing. The morning mist adds a magical touch to the scenery. Cable Car Ride: Taking the cable car to Tianzi Mountain is an adventure in itself. The panoramic views from the cabin are stunning, allowing you to soak in the grandeur of the landscape. Glass Bridge: Walking on the glass bridge over the Grand Canyon is both nerve-wracking and exhilarating. The adrenaline rush is unmatched, especially when you dare to look down! Organization: The park is well-organized with clear routes and signage. However, be prepared for large crowds, particularly during peak seasons. Recommendations: I recommend dedicating a few days to fully explore not only the Avatar Mountains but also other attractions in the park, such as the Golden Whip Stream and the Yellow Dragon Cave. Conclusion: Zhangjiajie is a must-visit destination for nature lovers and those seeking unique landscapes. It feels like stepping into another world full of wonder and inspiration.

Visiting Zhangjiajie National Park is a breathtaking experience that leaves a lasting impression. The park's stunning landscapes, featuring towering sandstone pillars, lush forests, and winding rivers, create a surreal atmosphere that feels almost otherworldly. The Avatar Hallelujah Mountain, famously inspiring the floating mountains in the movie "Avatar," is a must-see and offers spectacular views. The glass bridge at Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon, one of the highest and longest in the world, provides a thrilling experience for those brave enough to walk across. The cable car ride up Tianmen Mountain offers panoramic vistas and a sense of tranquility as you ascend through the clouds. The exhilarating walk along the glass skywalk is another highlight, providing a unique perspective of the park's dramatic cliffs. Zhangjiajie National Park is well-maintained, with clear trails and helpful signage. The staff are friendly and knowledgeable, adding to the overall positive experience. Whether you're an avid hiker, a photography enthusiast, or simply looking to connect with nature, Zhangjiajie National Park offers something for everyone. Be prepared for some steep climbs and bring good walking shoes to fully enjoy the adventure.

Zhangjiajie National Forest Park is a hidden gem that offers a unique blend of natural beauty and cultural heritage. The park's towering sandstone pillars and deep ravines create a dramatic landscape that feels almost otherworldly, while the area's rich history and culture add depth and meaning to the experience. Visitors can take a range of hikes and cable car rides that offer different perspectives of the park, from peaceful strolls through the forests to thrilling adventures that take you high above the treetops. The park is also home to a range of rare wildlife and plant species, adding to the sense of discovery and wonder. What sets Zhangjiajie National Forest Park apart from other natural wonders is the sense of spirituality and harmony that pervades the area, making it the perfect place to reflect and find inner peace. Whether you're a nature lover or a cultural enthusiast, Zhangjiajie National Forest Park is a must-visit destination that will leave you feeling inspired and uplifted by the beauty and diversity of our world.

When you first set eyes on Zhangjiajie National Forest Park in Hunan province, it's certainly not difficult to see how filmmaker James Cameron was able to draw inspiration from it. Cameron's box office hit, Avatar, could well have been set in this area of stunning natural beauty, its many unique pillar-like rock formations looking like some incredible alien landscape right out of a sci-fi movie (one of the tallest pillars, standing at an impressive 1,080-meters, has in fact been renamed "Avatar Hallelujah Mountain"). This is one of the lesser known places to visit in China. In addition to its many natural wonders, which can best be explored as part of an organized tour, the park boasts a number of new man-made attractions. The first to be built was the Bailong Elevator, aka the "Hundred Dragons Sky Lift." Elevating groups of up to 50 people 326 meters skyward in under two minutes, it's an impressive structure, and one that offers dramatic views all the way. Also notable is the Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon Glass Bridge, opened in 2016 and heralded as the world's highest and tallest pedestrian bridge. Standing 300 meters above the ground and extending 430 meters along a spectacular cliff face, it's an attraction that's definitely not recommended for the faint of heart but one of the best things to do if you are looking to add a little adventure to your day.

The park’s response to this is to arm park employees with slingshots so they can shoot rocks at the monkeys to scare them away. I recognize that China has never been progressive in terms of environmental protection/animal treatment, but I expected better than this.

Zhangjiajie Glass Bridge Zhangjiajie Glass Bridge is a bridge inZhangjiajie, China, above the Wulingyuan area. The bridge, built as an attraction for tourists, is glass-bottomed and is transparent. When it opened it was the longest and tallest glass bottomed bridge in the world. The bridge, opened to the public on August 20, 2016, measures 430 metres in total length and 6 metres in breadth, and is suspended about 260 metres above the ground.[1] The bridge spans the canyon between two mountain cliffs in Zhangjiajie National Forest Park in China's central Hunan province. It is designed to carry up to 800 visitors at a time. The bridge was designed by Israeli architect Haim Dotan.[2]To build the bridge, engineers erected 4 support pillars on the edges of the walls of the canyon. The bridge is made of a steel frame with more than 120 glass panels. Each of these panels is 3-layered and is a 2-inch-thick slab of tempered glass. There are 3 longswings attached to the underside of the bridge. Also there is a provision for making a 265 metre bungee-jump. This is considered to be highest such jump in the world.[3] According to the Management Committee of the Bridge, the bridge has set ten world records spanning its design and construction.[4] The record as longest glass bridge has since passed to a glass bridge in the Hongyagu Scenic Area, Hebei.[5]

The Zhangjiajie National Forest Park (Chinese: 湖南张家界国家森林公园; pinyin: Húnán Zhāngjiājiè Guójiā Sēnlín Gōngyuán; literally: "Hunan Zhangjiajie National Forest Park") is a unique national forest park located in Zhangjiajie City in northern Hunan Province in the People's Republic of China. It is one of several national parks within the Wulingyuan Scenic Area. In 1982 it was recognized as China's first national forest park with an area of 4,810 ha (11,900 acres). Zhangjiajie National Forest Park is part of a much larger 397.5 km2 (153.5 sq mi) Wulingyuan Scenic Area. In 1992, Wulingyuan was officially recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It was then approved by the Ministry of Land and Resources as Zhangjiajie Sandstone Peak Forest National Geopark (3,600 km2 (1,400 sq mi)) in 2001. In 2004, Zhangjiajie geopark was listed as a UNESCO global geopark. The most notable geographic features of the park are the pillar-like formations that are seen throughout the park. Although resembling karst terrain, this area is not underlain by limestones and is not the product of chemical dissolution, which is characteristic of limestone karst. They are the result of many years of physical, rather than chemical, erosion. Much of the weathering which forms these pillars are the result of expanding ice in the winter and the plants which grow on them. The weather is moist year round, and as a result, the foliage is very dense. The weathered material is carried away primarily by streams. These formations are a distinct hallmark of Chinese landscape, and can be found in many ancient Chinese paintings. One of the park's quartz-sandstone pillars, the 1,080-metre (3,540 ft) Southern Sky Column, had been officially renamed "Avatar Hallelujah Mountain" (阿凡达-哈利路亚山, pinyin: Āfándá hālìlùyà shān) in honor of the eponymous film in January 2010.[3] According to park officials, photographs from Zhangjiajie inspired the floating Hallelujah Mountains seen in the film.[4] The film's director and production designers said that they drew inspiration for the floating rocks from mountains from around the world, including those in Hunan province.

Es uno de los paisajes naturales más bonitos que he visto jamás. Sus formaciones rocosas verticales parecen surgir directamente de un mundo de fantasía. Uno de los mayores atractivos del parque es la montaña conocida como "Avatar Hallelujah Mountain", cuyo nombre original es "Pilar del Cielo del Sur", que es donde se grabó la película "Avatar". Además de las montañas, el parque cuenta con puentes naturales, barrancos, cascadas y bosques tropicales que albergan una rica biodiversidad. Su fauna incluye aves exóticas y también monos que se acercan pidiendo que les des de comer. También tiene teleféricos y ascensores panorámicos (uno de los cuales es el más alto del mundo). Otra experiencia emocionante es la del puente de cristal de Zhangjiajie (ubicado en el área de Wulingyuan), que ofrece vistas vertiginosas sobre el cañón. Y muy cerquita de este puente, que, además, es el puente de cristal con vistas panorámicas más largo del mundo, también se pueden coger barquitos para dar un paseo tranquilo por el río. En definitiva, se trata de un parque muy completito, con paisajes muy diferentes en cada sitio y que requiere unos 5 días enteros para conocer los más importantes de ellos.

Parc national de 264 hectares avec quelques 3000 pics, nous avons donc décidé de le faire en deux jours. nous avons réservé nos billets la veille pour les télécabines, les bus navettes et l'ascenseur, prix réduits pour les plus de 65 ans. Premier jour nous avons fait la partie Huangshi village, nous sommes rentrés par la porte sud et nous sommes allés jusqu'à la rivière à pied, nous l'avons longée sur 500 mètres et nous sommes revenus sur nos pas pour prendre la navette afin de rejoindre le télécabine, une fois au sommet nous avons fait le tour en passant par la pagode mais le temps nuageux nous a privé de la vue notamment le premier site de tournage d'avatar. Le deuxième jour nous avons fait la partie huanjiajie autre site du film avatar, nous sommes rentrés par la porte est et nous avons pris la navette pour aller directement à l'ascenseur, il y avait du monde mais dans l'ensemble c'était fluide un petit quart d'heure pour y accéder. La montée est impressionnante, les gens se collent tout de suite à la vitre pour filmer, trop de nuages pour nous donc pas vu grand chose. Nous avons pris une navette pour aller au parking suivant et de là nous avons fait la balade à pied jusqu'au parking d'après en passant par le premier pont, nous avons alterné les vues dans les nuages et sans nuages,ce qui nous a permis de comprendre l'idée des montagnes qui flottent dans les airs du film avatar. Ensuite nous avons pris la navette pour aller à Tianzi montain pour avoir la vue sur les pics, nous y avons déjeuné puis nous avons pris le télécabine pour retourner à la porte est. Deux bons jours de visite ou nous avons du jouer avec le temps , tout est bien organisé dans le parc ce qui rend la visite seraine, je vous recommande ce moment de détente et de découverte.

Le parc national de Zhangjiajie est un incontournable de la Chine si vous transitez par la région. Il se situe à 34 km au nord de la ville du même nom, facilement accessible en transport en commun (bus) ou taxi. Nous avons opté pour la course en taxi qui est relativement bon marché [entre 50 et 70 ¥]. Nous avions réservé nos tickets avec notre hotel. Le ticket est valable pendant 4 jours tant le parc est grand et coute 223 ¥ avec les bus à l'intérieur du parc inclus. Ne restant pas longtemps dans la région, nous avons condensé notre visite du parc en une demi-journée. Entrés à 12h, nous en sommes partis vers 17h30 après avoir visité, à nos yeux, ce qui semblait essentiel. Nous sommes entrés par la porte de l'est et nous avons pris un minibus en direction des montagnes de Tianzi. Du parking, nous avons pris un téléphérique (79 ¥ par personne et par trajet) pour nous emmener directement au sommet. De là, nous avons pu admirer différents points de vue sur les aiguilles de Tianzi, la beauté du paysage. il y a d'innombrables points de vue, tous plus beaux les uns que les autres. C'est époustouflant. Nous avons fait le choix de redescendre à pied, via un sentier à l'ombre, entretenu mais moussu. Les marches sont glissantes. Après 1h30 de descente, nous avons repris un bus le long de la route direction l'autre partie du parc, à savoir Yangjiajie et la fameuse Halleluia Mountain. Nous avons pris l'ascenseur de bailong (65¥ / personne et par trajet) pour monter et redescendre puisque le sentier que nous voulions prendre était fermé (Golden Whip Stream). L'ascenseur en lui-même est un spectacle. Avec une vitesse de pointe inégalée pour un ascenseur situé en extérieur, on est vite au sommet. L'effet wahou est intense. Là-haut, nous avons pris un bus nous menant aux points d'intérêt à savoir la montagne Halleluia qui a inspiré les décors du film Avatar, la passerelle au-dessus du vide, des points de vue sur des arêtes et aiguilles sculptées par le temps et l'érosion. Une vraie forêt de pierre à couper le souffle. Nous avons passé au moins 2h30 dans cette zone mais il est largement possible d'en passer davantage. Ce parc est une d'une beauté inimaginable. Très bien entretenus, les sentiers permettent d'approcher des endroits les plus beaux et spectaculaires. C'est un incontournable de Zhangjiajie et nous aurions voulu pouvoir profiter davantage en y restant plus longtemps. Le retour au centre-ville se fait de la même manière que l'arrivée, c'est-à-dire en taxi ou bus.

👩‍🦳張家界8日D5 2026.1.13 #張家界國家森林公園(Zhangjiajie National Forest Park)位於張家界市武陵源區，總面積48.1平方千米，與一脈相連的索溪峪、天子山、楊家界三大自然保護區組成武陵源，地處武景山脈中段，是張武家界的核心區。地形是 #砂岩地形的特殊類型，由產狀近水平的中、泥盆統石英砂岩為成景母岩，以流水侵蝕、重力崩塌、風化等作用力形成，棱角平直、高大石柱林為主的地貌景觀。屬北亞熱帶季風性濕潤氣候，年均氣溫17℃，以峰稱奇、以谷顯幽、以林見秀。有奇峰3千多座，如人如獸、器物，氣勢壯觀，有「奇峰三千，秀水八百」之美稱。主要景點有黃石寨、金鞭溪、袁家界、楊家界等。 1988年8月，列入國家重點風景名勝區；1992年12月，奇特的石英砂岩大峰林被聯合國列入 #世界自然遺產名錄；2004年2月列入 #世界地質公園；2007年列入中國首批國家5A級旅遊景區。 🏞命名：據明崇禎四年(1631)《張氏族譜》張再昌序言記載，明弘治年間(1488～1506)，朝廷因張萬聰指揮使鎮守永定衛大庸有功，將今張家界國家森林公園一帶“山林之地”，作為封賞賜給張萬聰。張萬聰第六代孫張再弘，被朝廷賜為團官，縣設衙署於張家界。從此成為張氏世襲之地，張家界由此得名。經張姓後裔“守業經營”，張家界舊時有大片原始次森林，1958年被闢為張家界林場。1982年9月，被國家計劃委員會正式命名。 🏞地形：張家界市位於湖南省西北部，北與湖北省鶴峰縣交界，地處武陵山脈東段，地勢由西北向東南。張家界地形在中國華南板塊大地構造背景和亞熱帶濕潤區內，由產狀近水平的中、泥盆統石英砂岩為成景母岩，以流水侵蝕、重力崩塌、風化等作用力形成的以棱角平直的、高大石柱林為主的地形景觀。在多種因素作用下，形成了平台、方山、石牆、石柱、天生橋與殘林等景觀類型。摘錄：百度

我的川湘行領隊說： 現在出外旅行能包就包能VIP就VIP 就可以省下不少（排隊等候)時間. 昨天和今天看到長長的排隊人龍，我們都能順利地走VIP通道和很快的搭上包車，真的省得非常多的時間。 然而能包能VIP卻未能得到老天爺的青睞 今天整天下雨，早上行程還算可以，下午在山上袁家界（張家界包括袁家界和楊家界）看阿凡達的幾個山峰，卻完全被雲霧繚繞遮住，只能依稀看出一點模樣。 非常殘念。 有人搭乘滑竿上下山的影片。 張家界導遊說： 張家界一年有兩百多天下雨。 三月底四月和11月比較適合過來，因為比較少下雨。
張家界風景區真的是一個讓人走進就會驚嘆的地方。整個景區以奇峰林立、雲霧繚繞而聞名，那種大自然鬼斧神工的震撼感，照片完全無法呈現。親眼看到那一根根直插天際的砂岩石柱，會讓人不由自主停下腳步，只想靜靜欣賞。可惜這次來訪遇到下雨的天氣雲霧茫茫！期待下次回訪

人生不到張家界, 百歲豈能稱老翁. 사람이 태어나 장가계를 가지 않았다면, 백 세가 되어도 늙었다 할 수 있겠는가? 내가 이걸 보다니! 일찍이 많은 사람들에게 비경(祕境）이라 불리던 곳이자, 중국이 자랑하는 국가삼림공원 중 하나입니다. 수많은 기암괴석이 빽빽히 자리한, 마치 무릉도원 같은 풍경 때문에 지금도 수많은 관광객이 방문하고 있습니다. 1년 중 200일 이상 비와 안개가 끼는 곳이라 운이 나쁘면 아무것도 보이지 않습니다만, 다행이 제가 방문했을 때는 매우 맑은 날씨어서 모든 풍경을 온전히 볼 수 있었습니다. 장가계의 핵심만 보는 데만 하루 종일 걸립니다. 그렇기에 장가계를 여유있게 즐기고 싶으신 분은 2~3일 일정을 추천드립니다. 입장권은 총 4일 유효합니다. 백룡 엘레베이터 등 삼림공원 내 모든 교통수단은 별도 요금입니다. 단, 셔틀버스는 무료입니다. 보통 동문 입장 > 천자산 케이블카 > 천자산 풍경구(어필봉 등) > 양가계 풍경구(일보등천 등) > 원가계 풍경구(천하제일교, 미혼대) > 백룡 엘레베이터 > 십리화랑 > 금편계곡 순으로 관광하면 하루 코스가 됩니다. 반대로 하셔도 상관 없고, 황석채 등을 보실 분은 별도 일정으로 잡으시길 추천드립니다. 장가계 버스터미널에서 무릉원까지 버스를 타면 쉽게 동문까지 올 수 있으며, 가격은 13위안입니다.

遊覽車抵達張家界，雨仍稀稀落落地下著，廣場旁有星巴克等餐飲店，導遊帶我們進入五A級武陵源風景區，天子山索道，我們搭纜車由此到上面山頭，有人興高彩烈很興奮，有人膽怯故作鎮定，我屬於後者，一段又一段地往上移動，兩旁山林地貌景觀大不相同，愈高霧氣愈濃，此時特殊山形漸顯，有時纜車完全被雲霧包圍，看不見周遭的一切，抵達山頭，我卸下緊張情緒。 雨仍下著，賀龍公園植物特別，觀景台是拍攝「御筆峰」的地方，可惜此時雲霧嬝繞、大雨紛飛，僅在想像中意會，但朦朧的美感環繞著，恰好。 雨稍緩和，霧濃，景觀台觀賞奇特山景，僅露出一些近端山形，導遊說大家一齊大聲叫喊，會把霧氣吹散的，我們整團一齊大叫「啊~」，持續喊叫多次，說也奇怪，前方雲霧竟漸漸散開，一見有效，其他旅遊團也加入我們喊叫的行列，許多的山都漸漸看到其面貌，山谷間仍飄有一些霧氣，像仙境般，聽現場其他導遊說，這情景他帶團六次才首見，特別的美，果真是世界級的景觀。 中午，我們在「阿凡達生態餐廳」用餐，餐後繼續欣賞奇山怪石之美，遊覽迷魂台、天下第一橋後，來到電影阿凡達的懸浮山原型-乾坤柱，遊客們一路看了這麼多相類似的奇景後，內心似乎稍微平靜，有點審美疲乏了，左看是奇山，右看亦是奇山。 遊區內搭乘交通車往返各景點，駕駛師傅開車技巧很好，山區彎道不用減速，有點小驚嚇，我們來到十里畫廊，原以為是參觀畫作，後來才知道是搭乘小火車，觀看被命名的天然景觀，真如詩如畫。 張家界的奇山景觀，不管是天晴、霧景或雪景都是絕美，非常值得來觀賞。

以奇峰怪石與石英砂岩峰林聞名，成排山巒拔地而起，在雲霧環繞下宛如一幅流動的山水畫，視覺震撼且極具辨識度。園區範圍廣大，步道規劃完整，行走其間可同時感受峽谷的深邃、溪流的清澈與森林的蓊鬱層次。清晨或雨後最迷人，雲海翻湧於峰林之間，光影變化讓人百看不膩。整體生態保存良好，空氣清新，步行時能明顯感受到遠離城市的放鬆感。無論是健行、攝影，或單純沉浸在自然之中，都能獲得深刻體驗，是一處會讓人回味再三、值得細細探索的自然景觀。

バスを降りてすぐ壮観な景色が目の前に現れました。昔水墨山水画の掛け軸を見たとき、本当にこんな風景があるのかと疑っていましたが、本当に存在していたのです。 ・金鞭渓は張家界国家森林公園内の全長5.7kmの渓谷です。「世界で一番綺麗な峡谷」と呼ばれているそうです。峡谷の両側には金鞭岩などの高い岩峰がそそり立っています。
风景还不错，就像小学课文里面写的那样美，据说电影《阿凡达》在袁家界取过景。景区内可乘坐环保观光巴士很舒适方便，适合腿脚不方便的游客。山顶的食物比较贵（包括KFC），大约是正常市场价的3-5倍，出发前可以自带干粮以备不时之需。另外景区有很多国家二级保护动物野生猕猴，喂食以及合影时尽量注意人身以及财产安全，我们一起的游客就有被抓伤的。

C’est un magnifique parc naturel. Il y a énormément de chemins mais il faut être un petit peut sportif car toutes les montées sont faites en marche d’escaliers. Ce ne sont pas du tout des chemins en terre mais goudronné. Sinon il y a aussi des ascenseurs ou des télécabines. Tout dépend l’entrée que vous prenez. Il existe des passes pour plusieurs jours mais le parc est très cher. Il n’y a pas de carte d’accès mais c’est votre empreinte digitale qui fait fois. Sinon dans la ville personne ne parle anglais et encore moins français. Ça a été le parcours du combattant pour y arriver en bus. Télécharger Google translater et vous devriez vous débrouiller. Dans le parc il y a un petit peut partout des stands pour y acheter à boire ou à manger mais il n’acceptent pas la carte de crédit mais uniquement le cash.

멋진곳 한겨울에도 눈보기 힘든곳이지만 내가 갔을땐 눈꽃이 피어 더욱 환상적이였다, 한국인 어르신들이 가고싶어하는 곳이며 실제로도 많이들 관광으로 가는곳 , 유네스코 세계자연유산중 하나이며, 제대로 보려면 최소 일주일정도는 머물러야 하지않을까한다. 나는 팔순 부모님과 같이 효도관광으로 다녀왔고 편의 시설이 잘되어있어 나이드신 분들도 돌아다니기에 그리 불편하지않다, 무엇보다 풍경이 장관이다 일반적이지않은 지형지물.. 간간히 마주치는 원숭이들, 그 사이사이 만들어놓은 사람들을 위한 편의시설들, 꼭 가보길 권장한다. 가능하면 부모님과 같이가면 확실히 좋아하시리라본다.
Sublime, à voir absolument ! En revanche les prix des ascenseurs et télécabines est un peu abusé, surtout quand on a déjà payé un billet d’entrée dans le parc

정말 좋은 산입니다. 직접 자유여행으로 발로 걷고 타고 뛰면서 모든 구간을 등산한 뒤 팁으로는... 1. 산 정산위의 마을의 객잔에서 머물면서 다니자. - 산 위에는 많은 객잔이 있습니다. 근처에서 보급도 가능하고, 음식점도 맛집이 꽤 많습니다. 시설은 당연히 별로지만... 따뜻한 물에, 전기매트를 주니 살만 하더라구요. 당연하지만, 마을에서 걸어서 5분 거리로 장가계 공원 버스가 다닙니다. 드라이기는 필수입니다. 당연하다지만... 2. 황룡엘레베이터는 마지막 날에, qing xi 구역을 내려갈때만 쓰자. - 올라갈려는 사람이 많아서 못탑니다. 내려가려는 사람은 없어서 4명에서 타고 내려갔네요. 개꿀. 3. 한 구역당 5시간, 석양을 볼 생각은 하지 말자. - 버스 끊기면 답 안나옵니다. 객잔에 차 불러서 복귀해야하는데, 비싸요. 그러므로 황산같이, 산 위에서 머물면서 석양 / 일출 보기에는 난이도가 굉장히 높습니다. 특히 석양은 불가능해요. 애초에 라이트가 없고, 길도 험합니다. 그 외로는 산의 난이도는 하-중 정도의 쉬운 편이니 걱정 안하셔도 됩니다. 시간과 코스만 잘 정하시면, 버스타고 복귀하고 또 버스타고 공략하는 맛이 있어서 좋습니다.

Công viên rừng quốc gia Trương Gia Giới là một trong những công viên rừng cấp quốc gia đầu tiên ở Trung Quốc. Công viên thực sự là một "nhà kho" đúng nghĩa với trên 97% diện tích được bao phủ bởi hàng nghìn loại thực vật, trong đó có nhiều loài quý hiếm và đặc hữu. Khu bảo tồn thiên nhiên thung lũng Tố Khê nằm ở khu trung tâm của Vũ Lăng Nguyên và là khu vực có diện tích lớn nhất. Sương mù là khung cảnh thường gặp ở đây, điều này khiến cho cả thung lũng lúc nào cũng đắm chìm trong vẻ huyền bí mờ ảo, như lạc vào cõi tiên.

Één van de mooiste nationale parken ter wereld die ik ooit heb gezien. De uitzichten zijn buitenaards mooi. De wandelpaden zijn vrij rustig (de Chinezen houden niet van wandelen). Met een goede kaart, een behulpzame hotelreceptie en een vertaal-app is het heel makkelijk hier te reizen. Veel bussen, kabelbanen en wegwijzerbordjes. Hoogtepunt vond ik het uitzicht bij Yuanjiajie. Dit park is echt de moeite waard, ook als het niet 'op de route' ligt.
Прекрасный и интересный парк. Посещаю второй раз. Приятное впечатление. Рекомендую. По мотивам гор аллилуйя
